# ADR-0244: Derive coordination via naming convention, not a shared trait

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-05-29

**Context.** The #[serve]/Serve derive must discover and wire up methods generated by other derives (OpenApi, Metrics, HealthCheck, third-party extensions) on the same struct, across crate boundaries, without a registry or linker tricks.

**Decision.** Each derive generates a method whose name is the snake_case form of the PascalCase derive name (OpenApi -> openapi, HealthCheck -> health_check), and Serve emits calls to Self::<name>() by name. Coordination is purely by naming convention: no registry, no inventory crate, no ctor-style linker tricks, no shared trait dependency.

**Alternatives rejected.**
- *Trait-based discovery (a marker trait like ServerExtension that each derive implements, with Serve calling <T as ServerExtension>::layer())* — A single type can only implement a trait once, so multiple extensions on the same struct would need associated types, HLists, or other machinery to compose; it also forces every extension author to depend on server-less-core for the trait definition. The naming convention avoids version coupling across crates and composition limits.

**Consequences.** Extension authors must follow PascalCase-derive -> snake_case-method exactly; typos cause confusing method-not-found compile errors at the generated call site rather than at the extension. Mitigated by documentation, cargo expand, and a possible future #[server_less_extension] helper macro. The system stays free of shared runtime state and cross-crate dependency coupling.
